**Shortcut:** `Envision project` · **Skill:** `wf-envision`

Imagine what this product could make possible for people and why that future matters. Seek relevant financial and nonfinancial value; strategy explains the choices, sacrifices and path from today's reality. Useful horizons make that path credible.

## Scope and working method

Write one coherent vision by default: the existing canonical location, otherwise root `VISION.md`, titled `<Project>: Vision and Roadmap` when new. Honor requested filenames and preserve existing titles, valid material, working references and unrelated edits. Integrate consequential research, citations, assumptions, contrary evidence and open choices into the argument. Full review accounting belongs in the delivery response; the vision keeps a one- or two-line status naming the review date, reviewed revision labels, roles actually run, pending finding count and unreviewed changes, or stating unknown/not reviewed. Identify revisions with dated labels. Explicit project/operator evidence-location instructions override this default. Existing siblings do not authorize new files, overwrite, retirement or silent invalidation. Substantial separately reusable research can justify a companion only with its concrete purpose stated beforehand; honor a single-document request.

A discussion, prompt-writing request or read-only review writes nothing. Authoring and review do not adopt a vision, create lifecycle records or grant implementation, approval, deployment, commit or publication authority. Do not expand network access, run setup or change the environment. External research stays within authorized scope; disclose missing evidence or request necessary access without silently adding network research to a local-only engagement. Preserve operator-owned strategic choices and existing adoption.

Read phase guidance only at the applicable transition below, before its dependent action. These are project-local operating instructions, not vision-output siblings. Retain needed context; reread only if materially changed or unavailable. Missing, unreadable or conflicting required guidance stops that dependent step: report the exact path and conflict or access gap. Do not substitute canonical guidance around local policy, skip the step, invent coverage or automatically run setup/upgrade. Independent authorized work may continue; these core boundaries always apply.

## 1. Establish the brief

Reuse conversation and project context to establish ambition, beneficiaries, desired progress, horizon, constraints and deliverable. Reuse concrete operator or beneficiary experience; ask for a decision-relevant missing example instead of inventing daily use. Explore who adopts, pays for or sustains the product, why now, deliberate non-goals and what failure means only where these affect choices. Personal usefulness, open adoption and income can coexist. A hobby or small team constrains pace without automatically capping the destination. Do not require a market choice before helping explore futures.

When the product belongs to an existing organization, establish its role using known company context; the research phase supplies proportional grounding. Distinguish commitments from current positioning. The portfolio may enable a larger future without defining its ceiling. Standalone projects need no company discovery.

With sufficient context, state your interpretation and proceed. Combine genuine blockers, inferred-brief readback and review notice in one brief exchange; defer nonblocking questions as explicit uncertainties. Silence is not selection. Do not impose a questionnaire, twelve-month horizon, unlimited resources, commercialization, cloud, autonomous agents, platform scope or a fixed horizon count.

For new/substantial visions, select advisory product strategy, domain/application workflow, senior architecture and independent challenge coverage. A substantial revision changes purpose, beneficiary, horizons or their order; other edits use affected reviews proportionately. Scale depth by stakes, maturity and uncertainty. Narrowing needs a brief-specific reason, never lower author effort alone; high stakes or uncertainty keep the default unless the operator directs otherwise. Honor explicit scope, additions or omission. State selected roles, consequential specialties and expected effort without invented cost/duration estimates; reuse an explicit scope without another approval. Selected roles need separate independent contexts, or honest disclosure of shared context and missing independence. No chair or consensus process is required.

When revising an existing vision, **read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/revision.prompt.md` before revising it**.

## 2. Ground the need and starting point

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/research.prompt.md` before gathering or assessing evidence.** Build a compact diagnosis of desired progress, obstacles, pivotal insight and timely opportunity. Distinguish observations, interpretations and hypotheses. Repository facts establish capability, not demand; missing primary research permits a provisional vision with visible gaps.

Separate the project's originating problem, binding operator commitments, present implementation/deployment, deferred capabilities and proposed changes of product responsibility. Current requirements remain binding until changed; neither dismiss them as accidents nor promote a first deployment into permanent destiny. Name new obligations introduced by expansion and consequential decisions for the operator.

Classify relevant capabilities as working, working with limitations, genuinely missing or not yet established. Attribute operating experience separately from reproduced behavior. Preserve demonstrated strengths as foundations; lack of broad evaluation does not make them absent. Carry verified classifications through the draft and immediate priorities, changing them only with new evidence. Resolve consequential inventory/source/draft/reviewer disagreements through targeted checks or explicit uncertainty, without another broad audit.

## 3. Explore, then recommend

When the destination is open, **before drafting the recommended destination**, develop each serious alternative through a comparably concrete beneficiary experience, distinctive value, consequential obligations and uncertainty. Compare product futures, not only engines, packaging, distribution routes or business models. Explain what people do, what the system does, where human judgment remains and what people receive. Give alternatives enough substance to judge fairly; no fixed count, equal-length requirement or exhaustive research is needed. Apply missing and contrary evidence consistently, including to the favored option.

When the operator has chosen the destination, preserve it; do not manufacture alternatives or reopen strategy by rote. Where ambition is requested, seriously examine transformative capacity beyond today's backlog without assuming bigger is better. Explain the recommendation and sacrifices, financial and nonfinancial value, costs, adoption and sustainability. Compare manual practice, competing products, do-it-yourself or doing nothing where consequential. Distinguish a useful benefit from a mechanism that could sustain its value; do not invent an optimum or moat. Enduring usefulness and stewardship may matter more than excluding competitors.

Place inferred beneficiary, scope and destination choices near the recommendation, with implications and unresolved decisions. Treat an interesting reviewer hypothesis as a hypothesis until supported or selected. Future capacity is aspiration, not established capability or a guarantee. Missing present proof does not disprove ambition; contrary evidence still matters. Reducing the destination is an operator-owned strategic choice, not a factual correction. A small first advance must support or test the larger future.

## 4. Write the vision and roadmap

Deliver the argument **summary-first**: a short, repeatable destination statement in beneficiary language, then a concise roadmap overview before detailed reasoning. The reader should understand the distinctive future, why it was chosen and how useful stages make it real. Alternatives-first authoring does not require alternatives-first presentation. Keep the operative brief where it explains consequential choices, not as an interview transcript. Consolidate general caveats while keeping decision-specific limits visible. A concise appendix is optional; do not concatenate research notes and review transcripts or bury all evidence there. There is no vision word ceiling: scale depth to stakes, maturity and uncertainty.

Assess value, usability, feasibility and viability at the destination. Work backward from the ultimate experience to capabilities, foundations and unresolved breakthroughs, then forward through useful horizons. Each horizon needs a beneficiary outcome, independent intermediate value if later stages never arrive, consequential risk reduced, and evidence for advancing or reconsidering. Near horizons have concrete end-to-end demonstrations, exit criteria and failure conditions; an unchanged baseline must fail a new-capability demonstration. Distant horizons retain outcomes, assumptions and provisional conditions with decreasing precision. Qualitative conditions are valid; invent no distant dates, targets or commitments. Retain justified operator timing as aspiration or constraint. Research stages name uncertainty, stopping conditions and enabled value; activity or infrastructure completion alone is not product value.

Connect necessary research, adoption, distribution, funding, partnerships, operating practices and team capability to engineering outcomes. Show dependencies, parallel opportunities, critical path and timing assumptions, including nontechnical prerequisites. Explain components, state ownership, interfaces and instrumentation where they clarify the path; keep tickets outside the vision. Architecture, security, modernization, reliability and performance belong where they enable value, not as mandatory audit categories. Unlimited-resource analysis, if useful, explains which experiments or specialists help and which bottlenecks remain; workers do not imply proportional progress.

Explain endurance and adaptability at the depth risk warrants: durable principles versus current rules, consequential sources of truth, contracts, trust boundaries, execution locations, integrations, maintenance, feedback and human decisions. Use a diagram when it clarifies foundations. Address costly-to-reverse commitments, replaceable boundaries and migration without speculative extensibility. For major assumption failure, say what remains useful, what changes and which decision returns to the operator. Revisit when exit evidence, assumptions or beneficiary evidence changes; proposed destination changes stay explicit.

State how success and failure would be recognized. Use proportionate beneficiary outcome measures and guardrails, necessary baselines and observation limits; targets are not results and activity counts are not success. Map risky assumptions to cheap discriminating experiments and evidence that would change a decision. Research guidance supplies technical-comparison and evaluation detail when consequential.

End with ordered immediate advances tied to the ultimate demonstration and nearer horizons. Explain each observed gap/opportunity, current capability, incremental outcome, timing, dependencies and continuation evidence. Distinguish preserving, extending, investigating/validating and building; uncertain evidence may warrant validation rather than rebuilding. Choose useful priorities, not a quota or duplicate backlog.

## 5. Review and deliver

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/review.prompt.md` before briefing reviewers or repairing findings.** Give independent reviewers their applicable remit and necessary brief/evidence, not the whole authoring workflow by rote. The author owns revisions; reviews remain read-only and advisory. Use one initial pass, one bounded repair and affected-reviewer verification, then report remaining findings without another automatic repair loop. Unavailable capability means disclosed pending coverage, never impersonated review or host reconfiguration. Keep the compact status honest even when review is omitted.

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/delivery.prompt.md` before final validation, status and adoption handoff.** Deliver one usable argument, accurate reviewed-versus-delivered revision coverage and material open decisions. Explain the direction, value, horizons, ordered immediate advances and evidence limits without starting subsequent work.

I read your ambition as making field observations useful beyond the moment of capture, while using a modest pilot to discover a sustainable path. Your working offline notes, photos and CSV export give us a foundation; the beneficiary and ongoing responsibility remain open.

Three futures seem worth considering. These are imagined experiences, not validated needs:

- **An observer’s lasting field companion.** Someone returns to a site years later and can recover what they saw, compare observations and assemble an understandable account. Trailbook connects records across visits; the observer judges their meaning. The value is personal continuity and better-informed observation. This would prioritize retrieval and comparison, with obligations around durable storage, recovery and portability. We do not yet know what people struggle to recover or whether their existing notebooks already suffice.
- **A shared memory for rotating teams.** A newcomer arrives able to understand previous observations, unresolved questions and why earlier volunteers made particular judgments. Trailbook preserves context, provenance and corrections; people decide what is credible. The value is knowledge that survives turnover. This would prioritize handover and shared interpretation, requiring access rules and someone to steward disputed or stale material. We do not yet know whether handover is a pressing problem or who would sustain that stewardship.
- **A system for coordinating fieldwork.** Volunteers see what needs attention, take responsibility and hand completed work back to a coordinator. Trailbook connects assignments to observations; humans set priorities and resolve exceptions. The value is more reliable collective coverage. This would prioritize planning and accountability, bringing stronger reliability, support and coordination obligations. We do not yet know whether teams want to depend on Trailbook for this or whether existing coordination practices work well.

My tentative recommendation is to explore **shared team memory** first: it could turn today’s records into enduring collective value without immediately taking responsibility for organizing the work. That is a hypothesis, not a selected destination. Choosing it would defer coordination benefits and make stewardship a central pilot question. A small handover trial using existing exports could test whether a new volunteer gains useful understanding and how much upkeep that requires, before costly commitments.

Which future should anchor the vision—individual continuity, shared team memory, coordination, or a combination with one primary purpose? You can also defer the choice and ask for evidence first; that would make comparing real recovery, handover and coordination difficulties the next step.

Mosaic could help people turn scattered creative fragments into work they understand, develop and choose to share. My provisional recommendation is a personal creative workspace that helps someone carry an idea from sketch to considered revision, while testing whether trusted critique deserves to become a central purpose. You have not selected that destination; the recommendation and roadmap below remain exploratory.

The possible path is to make returning to an idea useful, then help its author develop it, then—only if the evidence and your later choice support it—make critique a dependable part of that process. Each step should leave something valuable even if the larger future changes.

Two futures merit serious consideration:

- **A personal creative practice.** Someone returns to a collection of sketches, finds the thinking behind an unfinished idea, compares variations and decides what to pursue. Mosaic would connect relevant notes and versions while leaving interpretation, taste and final choices with the author. The result would be a body of work whose development remains understandable over time. This could support continuity and creative independence, but requires dependable preservation, retrieval and export. We do not yet know whether difficulty developing ideas, rather than simply capturing them, is a significant unmet need; folders and a notebook may already suffice.
- **A trusted critique practice.** Someone selects a work in progress, explains the kind of help wanted and invites chosen peers to respond to particular parts. Mosaic would preserve the context of feedback and subsequent revisions; people would judge the advice and retain authority over their work. The result could be better creative decisions and sustained learning between collaborators. This introduces responsibility for consent, access, shared state and harmful or unwanted feedback, as well as the practical burden of finding willing critics. We do not yet know whether structured exchanges would improve on existing conversations or whether participation would persist.

I provisionally favor the personal direction because it can deliver value without coordinating other participants and builds on the local collection described in your brief. That is a sequencing judgment, not proof of stronger demand. It sacrifices the possibility of making relationships and collective learning Mosaic's defining value from the outset. Neither direction currently has evidence of willingness to pay or a sustainable maintenance model.

A cheap collaboration test would use existing sketches and ordinary messages: invite a few willing creators to request one specific kind of critique from a trusted peer, then observe whether the exchange changes a creative decision and whether both sides want to repeat it. Record useful advice, misunderstandings, effort and declined invitations. If feedback adds little beyond their normal conversation, defer dedicated collaboration features; if repeated exchanges produce valued revisions, bring the destination choice back to you. This proposes a test; it does not start one.

The later choice controls whether the roadmap prioritizes private continuity or reliable shared critique, and whether Mosaic assumes ongoing responsibilities to multiple participants. First, validate the personal development problem; next, test critique's added value; then choose which future merits a fuller roadmap. The brief establishes local sketch and note collection only; these proposed capabilities and benefits are unverified. No research or advisory reviews were performed for this excerpt, and no vision has been adopted or implementation authorized.

# Volunteer Group: Vision and Roadmap — Opening Excerpt

**Vision statement.** Make this volunteer group’s accumulated experience usable by each incoming coordinator, so leadership can change without losing the reasons behind past decisions. A new coordinator should be able to reconstruct what happened, understand what still matters and trace that understanding to the group’s historical meeting notes, without depending on a past leader to explain them. The enduring value is continuity: preserving the group’s ability to act thoughtfully as its volunteers change.

**Roadmap overview.** Build from the local note search described in the brief. First, observe incoming coordinators using small, manually prepared examples of a cited timeline and a decision index to answer a real handover question. Use their ability to reach a supported answer, recognize gaps and proceed without a former leader to choose the next useful presentation. Then make that selected experience repeatable across handovers, with a lightweight practice for recording new decisions and correcting misleading interpretations. Each stage should leave coordinators better able to use the existing record, even if later work stops.

The destination is already selected: continuity for this group. The unresolved choice concerns how best to reach it. If neither presentation improves on search alone, retain the search capability and investigate what context the notes lack before choosing further work. Commercial team management is outside this direction. This excerpt proposes a path; it does not adopt a VISION.md or authorize implementation. Advisory review is omitted for this requested opening-only exercise.

# Mosaic: Vision and Roadmap — Exploratory Opening Excerpt

**Provisional vision statement.** Mosaic should help people turn their scattered creative traces into a body of work they can understand and carry forward. A creator should be able to return to sketches and notes, recover the intentions behind them, discover connections and choose what to develop next while retaining ownership of the work and judgment over its direction. Its enduring purpose would be to make personal creative growth cumulative, so promising ideas remain available beyond the moment that produced them.

**Roadmap overview.** Begin with the local collection capability described in the brief and test whether returning to a small collection helps a creator resume an unfinished idea. Next, explore ways to connect related material and preserve the creator’s own account of its development. In parallel, a cheap, manual critique trial can establish whether an invited collaborator adds enough value to warrant a different destination. Shared critique remains contingent on that evidence and a later operator choice.

Two futures deserve consideration. In a personal creative workspace, the creator revisits earlier fragments, Mosaic helps surface connections and preserve context, and the creator decides what those connections mean. The value is continuity and renewed creative momentum; the obligations include reliable preservation and respectful handling of private material. Whether the collection actually improves creative progress remains unproven. In a collaborative critique space, a creator selects work to share, Mosaic would keep feedback attached to its context, and the creator decides which advice to accept. The value is a useful outside perspective; the added obligations include sharing consent, access control and practices that sustain constructive participation. Whether people will contribute useful feedback remains unproven.

The provisional recommendation favors personal creative continuity because it develops the existing local collection into a coherent beneficiary experience with fewer new social obligations. It sacrifices collaboration as the central organizing purpose. Before settling that choice, one creator could share a small selection with a trusted peer through an existing channel, then compare the usefulness of the resulting next step with a solo revisit. Useful feedback plus a desire to repeat the exchange would support further exploration, not establish demand. Choosing collaborative critique later would change the beneficiaries, responsibilities and horizon order. No destination has been selected, no vision adopted and no implementation authorized; this requested draft includes no interview or advisory review.

# 179 - Envision Project

**Applicable when:** any project. Establish or revise an ambitious product vision and an adaptable roadmap through useful technical and nontechnical advances. This is artifact authoring, not implementation planning or autonomous execution.

**Shortcut:** `Envision project` · **Skill:** `wf-envision`

Imagine what this product could make possible for people and why that future matters. Seek relevant financial and nonfinancial value; strategy explains the choices, sacrifices and path from today's reality. Useful horizons make that path credible.

## Scope and working method

Write one coherent vision by default: the existing canonical location, otherwise root `VISION.md`, titled `<Project>: Vision and Roadmap` when new. Honor requested filenames and preserve existing titles, valid material, working references and unrelated edits. Integrate consequential research, citations, assumptions, contrary evidence and open choices into the argument. Full review accounting belongs in the delivery response; the vision keeps a one- or two-line status naming the review date, reviewed revision labels, roles actually run, pending finding count and unreviewed changes, or stating unknown/not reviewed. Identify revisions with dated labels. Explicit project/operator evidence-location instructions override this default. Existing siblings do not authorize new files, overwrite, retirement or silent invalidation. Substantial separately reusable research can justify a companion only with its concrete purpose stated beforehand; honor a single-document request.

A discussion, prompt-writing request or read-only review writes nothing. Authoring and review do not adopt a vision, create lifecycle records or grant implementation, approval, deployment, commit or publication authority. Do not expand network access, run setup or change the environment. External research stays within authorized scope; disclose missing evidence or request necessary access without silently adding network research to a local-only engagement. Preserve operator-owned strategic choices and existing adoption.

Read phase guidance only at the applicable transition below, before its dependent action. These are project-local operating instructions, not vision-output siblings. Retain needed context; reread only if materially changed or unavailable. Missing, unreadable or conflicting required guidance stops that dependent step: report the exact path and conflict or access gap. Do not substitute canonical guidance around local policy, skip the step, invent coverage or automatically run setup/upgrade. Independent authorized work may continue; these core boundaries always apply.

## 1. Establish the brief

Reuse conversation and project context to establish ambition, beneficiaries, desired progress, horizon, constraints and deliverable. Reuse concrete operator or beneficiary experience; ask for a decision-relevant missing example instead of inventing daily use. Explore who adopts, pays for or sustains the product, why now, deliberate non-goals and what failure means only where these affect choices. Personal usefulness, open adoption and income can coexist. A hobby or small team constrains pace without automatically capping the destination. Do not require a market choice before helping explore futures.

When the product belongs to an existing organization, establish its role using known company context; the research phase supplies proportional grounding. Distinguish commitments from current positioning. The portfolio may enable a larger future without defining its ceiling. Standalone projects need no company discovery.

With sufficient context, state your interpretation and proceed. Combine genuine blockers, inferred-brief readback and review notice in one brief exchange; defer nonblocking questions as explicit uncertainties. Silence is not selection. Do not impose a questionnaire, twelve-month horizon, unlimited resources, commercialization, cloud, autonomous agents, platform scope or a fixed horizon count.

For new/substantial visions, select advisory product strategy, domain/application workflow, senior architecture and independent challenge coverage. A substantial revision changes purpose, beneficiary, horizons or their order; other edits use affected reviews proportionately. Scale depth by stakes, maturity and uncertainty. Narrowing needs a brief-specific reason, never lower author effort alone; high stakes or uncertainty keep the default unless the operator directs otherwise. Honor explicit scope, additions or omission. State selected roles, consequential specialties and expected effort without invented cost/duration estimates; reuse an explicit scope without another approval. Selected roles need separate independent contexts, or honest disclosure of shared context and missing independence. No chair or consensus process is required.

When revising an existing vision, **read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/revision.prompt.md` before revising it**.

## 2. Ground the need and starting point

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/research.prompt.md` before gathering or assessing evidence.** Build a compact diagnosis of desired progress, obstacles, pivotal insight and timely opportunity. Distinguish observations, interpretations and hypotheses. Repository facts establish capability, not demand; missing primary research permits a provisional vision with visible gaps.

Separate the project's originating problem, binding operator commitments, present implementation/deployment, deferred capabilities and proposed changes of product responsibility. Current requirements remain binding until changed; neither dismiss them as accidents nor promote a first deployment into permanent destiny. Name new obligations introduced by expansion and consequential decisions for the operator.

Classify relevant capabilities as working, working with limitations, genuinely missing or not yet established. Attribute operating experience separately from reproduced behavior. Preserve demonstrated strengths as foundations; lack of broad evaluation does not make them absent. Carry verified classifications through the draft and immediate priorities, changing them only with new evidence. Resolve consequential inventory/source/draft/reviewer disagreements through targeted checks or explicit uncertainty, without another broad audit.

## 3. Explore, then recommend

When the destination is open, **before drafting the recommended destination**, develop each serious alternative through a comparably concrete beneficiary experience, distinctive value, consequential obligations and uncertainty. Compare product futures, not only engines, packaging, distribution routes or business models. Explain what people do, what the system does, where human judgment remains and what people receive. Give alternatives enough substance to judge fairly; no fixed count, equal-length requirement or exhaustive research is needed. Apply missing and contrary evidence consistently, including to the favored option.

When the operator has chosen the destination, preserve it; do not manufacture alternatives or reopen strategy by rote. Where ambition is requested, seriously examine transformative capacity beyond today's backlog without assuming bigger is better. Explain the recommendation and sacrifices, financial and nonfinancial value, costs, adoption and sustainability. Compare manual practice, competing products, do-it-yourself or doing nothing where consequential. Distinguish a useful benefit from a mechanism that could sustain its value; do not invent an optimum or moat. Enduring usefulness and stewardship may matter more than excluding competitors.

After concrete alternatives make the choice intelligible, guide remaining decisions that would materially change beneficiaries, product responsibility, destination, horizon order or operating commitments, before settling the recommendation or polishing dependent review material. Take one decision at a time in dependency order. Explain why it matters now, credible options through future experiences, effects on outcomes, roadmap and obligations, your recommendation and uncertainty, and reversibility. Invite a choice, combination, deferral or request for evidence; reflect the actual answer and its consequences before the next dependent step. Ordinary engineering details need no strategic interview.

Pause dependent recommendation/review work while such a choice is unanswered; continue useful independent evidence work. Honor exploratory-draft-first/no-interview requests with visibly contingent choices and a provisional draft; return to conversation within the requested scope. Research-dependent deferrals need a useful next test. Explicit acceptance of a recommended direction can select strategy; silence, review agreement or approval of wording alone cannot. Selection alone grants neither adoption nor implementation authority. Keep choices and reasons in the vision and response, not a new decision artifact.

Place inferred choices and remaining uncertainty near the recommendation. Treat an interesting reviewer hypothesis as a hypothesis until supported or selected. Future capacity is aspiration, not established capability or a guarantee. Missing present proof does not disprove ambition; contrary evidence still matters. Reducing the destination is an operator-owned strategic choice, not a factual correction. A small first advance must support or test the larger future.

## 4. Write the vision and roadmap

Lead the substantive content **summary-first** with one clearly identified, unified vision statement: a concise standalone paragraph expressing the project’s enduring purpose, the future it exists to make possible and why that matters to the people it serves. Make its ultimate meaning specific to this project; a slogan, feature list or blend of competing futures is insufficient. Preserve a selected destination. An authorized exploratory draft can state one coherent recommendation clearly labeled provisional; use the guided-decision step for incompatible choices within the requested interview scope. Follow the statement with a concise roadmap overview, then the supporting argument.

The reader should understand the distinctive future, why it was chosen and how useful stages make it real. Alternatives-first authoring does not require alternatives-first presentation. Keep the operative brief where it explains consequential choices, not as an interview transcript. Consolidate general caveats while keeping decision-specific limits visible. A concise appendix is optional; do not concatenate research notes and review transcripts or bury all evidence there. There is no vision word ceiling: scale depth to stakes, maturity and uncertainty.

Assess value, usability, feasibility and viability at the destination. Work backward from the ultimate experience to capabilities, foundations and unresolved breakthroughs, then forward through useful horizons. Each horizon needs a beneficiary outcome, independent intermediate value if later stages never arrive, consequential risk reduced, and evidence for advancing or reconsidering. Near horizons have concrete end-to-end demonstrations, exit criteria and failure conditions; an unchanged baseline must fail a new-capability demonstration. Distant horizons retain outcomes, assumptions and provisional conditions with decreasing precision. Qualitative conditions are valid; invent no distant dates, targets or commitments. Retain justified operator timing as aspiration or constraint. Research stages name uncertainty, stopping conditions and enabled value; activity or infrastructure completion alone is not product value.

Connect necessary research, adoption, distribution, funding, partnerships, operating practices and team capability to engineering outcomes. Show dependencies, parallel opportunities, critical path and timing assumptions, including nontechnical prerequisites. Explain components, state ownership, interfaces and instrumentation where they clarify the path; keep tickets outside the vision. Architecture, security, modernization, reliability and performance belong where they enable value, not as mandatory audit categories. Unlimited-resource analysis, if useful, explains which experiments or specialists help and which bottlenecks remain; workers do not imply proportional progress.

Explain endurance and adaptability at the depth risk warrants: durable principles versus current rules, consequential sources of truth, contracts, trust boundaries, execution locations, integrations, maintenance, feedback and human decisions. Use a diagram when it clarifies foundations. Address costly-to-reverse commitments, replaceable boundaries and migration without speculative extensibility. For major assumption failure, say what remains useful, what changes and which decision returns to the operator. Revisit when exit evidence, assumptions or beneficiary evidence changes; proposed destination changes stay explicit.

State how success and failure would be recognized. Use proportionate beneficiary outcome measures and guardrails, necessary baselines and observation limits; targets are not results and activity counts are not success. Map risky assumptions to cheap discriminating experiments and evidence that would change a decision. Research guidance supplies technical-comparison and evaluation detail when consequential.

End with ordered immediate advances tied to the ultimate demonstration and nearer horizons. Explain each observed gap/opportunity, current capability, incremental outcome, timing, dependencies and continuation evidence. Distinguish preserving, extending, investigating/validating and building; uncertain evidence may warrant validation rather than rebuilding. Choose useful priorities, not a quota or duplicate backlog.

## 5. Review and deliver

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/review.prompt.md` before briefing reviewers or repairing findings.** Give independent reviewers their applicable remit and necessary brief/evidence, not the whole authoring workflow by rote. The author owns revisions; reviews remain read-only and advisory. Use one initial pass, one bounded repair and affected-reviewer verification, then report remaining findings without another automatic repair loop. Unavailable capability means disclosed pending coverage, never impersonated review or host reconfiguration. Keep the compact status honest even when review is omitted.

**Read `docs/prompts/agents/envision/delivery.prompt.md` before final validation, status and adoption handoff.** Deliver one usable argument, accurate reviewed-versus-delivered revision coverage and material open decisions. Explain the direction, value, horizons, ordered immediate advances and evidence limits without starting subsequent work.

# Envision — Advisory review

Internal phase guidance before reviewer briefing or findings repair. Apply the core's authority and selected coverage.

The author coordinates but does not impersonate independent reviewers. Identify the draft with a dated revision label; retain its exact bytes and SHA-256 after its label/status are present. Give each worker that same draft, brief, sources, relevant uncertainties, write boundaries and applicable remit. Reviewers read source and vision without writing them. Parallel reads are useful; serialize author revisions. Supply only relevant authoring guidance alongside the selected role's required protocol.

Use project role instructions where present. Assignments are analytical responsibilities, not credentials, stakeholder representation or customer validation. Ground findings in the identified brief/evidence and separate observation from hypothesis. Read the unified opening statement on its own: can a reader explain this project’s purpose, intended future and beneficiary value, faithfully to the brief and its selected or provisional status? Then test the serious alternatives and recommendation, useful horizons and connection of immediate advances to the larger future. Product strategy and independent challenge also check that consequential choices received guided discussion or an honored deferral/no-interview request, and that actual operator answers shaped the recommendation rather than reviewer agreement.

| Responsibility | Examine |
| --- | --- |
| Product strategy | Distinctive value, transformative destination, choices/sacrifices, adoption and viability. Detect unevenly developed alternatives, asymmetric uncertainty, conflated product scopes and deployment assumptions promoted into destiny; assess recommendation quality and immediate priorities. |
| Domain/application workflow | End-to-end fit, obligations, constraints and adoption. Distinguish operating experience from imagined workflows and identify missing beneficiary evidence. |
| Senior architecture | Current-capability accuracy, breakthroughs versus foundations, dependency order, ownership, interfaces, trust boundaries, credible transition and adaptability. |
| Independent challenge | Failure modes, unsupported certainty, contrary evidence and stronger alternatives; challenge unequal exploration, conflated scope and asymmetric demands for proof without choosing the operator's strategy. |

For company-backed products, product strategy and domain reviewers also challenge organizational fit, beneficiary evidence and whether existing positioning constrained ambition without justification. Architecture examines consequential portfolio dependencies and ownership boundaries. Distinguish strategic proposals from authority to change company commitments; add no separate review ceremony.

Add finance/economics when funding, cost to serve or sustainability shapes choices; security when trust/authority matters; reliability when recovery determines value; UX for consequential interaction uncertainty. Explain consequential omissions. Counts and role labels do not prove these questions were answered.

Architecture uses `docs/agents/architecture-reviewer.md` or the project's role, with seed `214-architecture-reviewer.prompt.md` as fallback. Independent challenge uses standalone Red-team review (`docs/prompts/red-team-review.prompt.md` and `docs/agents/specialists/red-team.md`; fallback seeds `177-red-team-review.prompt.md` and `225-red-team.prompt.md`), an appropriate lens and its required output. Preserve applicable independence/execution protocols and disclose shared author framing and model limitations.

Archetypes can be internal thinking techniques; they add no default roster, chair or consensus. Use plain responsibility/perspective labels in stakeholder-facing vision prose and status, without fictional/historical character performance. An explicitly requested standalone Archetype Council follows `docs/prompts/archetype-council.prompt.md`, full seed `236-archetype-council.prompt.md` and its chair instructions unchanged. Account for that selected form and actual execution separately; informal lenses are not a completed Council, and proportionate scope does not relax its protocol.

Correct false capability claims, broken reasoning, unsupported certainty and dependencies while preserving ambition and genuine contrary evidence. Proposed destination reductions remain operator decisions; reviewer hypotheses do not become adopted strategy. Continue within selected scope without routine reapproval; material scope/authority or unresolved strategic changes return to the operator. Synthesis, majority opinion and consensus grant no strategic authority.

Collect initial findings before editing, apply canonical dispositions with reasons and make one bounded author repair. Affected reviewers then verify the identified revised draft against prior findings and actual changes, supplied as claims to check rather than predetermined resolved verdicts. A no-new-finding follow-up is verification, not proof of uselessness, convergence or efficacy. After verification, stop substantive author repairs and report pending actionable findings/decisions. Later explicit operator direction can authorize another revision; identify its changed coverage and any focused follow-up actually performed. Updating honest delivery-status metadata does not authorize another substantive repair.

Generic role instructions about delivery-wave records apply only in that lifecycle. Here, create no wave records or `council-readiness`/`council-delivery` approvals and call no Prepare, Review wave or review-approval tools. Vision review replaces no implementation gate. Credible security issues go to a specialist; red-team issues no security signoff.

Unavailable workers, required role instructions or review capability leave that coverage pending. Continue useful authorized drafting/advice, label author self-checks honestly and disclose omitted coverage; never reconfigure the host or claim an unavailable review passed. Missing/conflicting Envision phase guidance still stops its dependent step under the core rule.

Planning leaves vision/review artifacts unchanged, adds no tracker, mandatory section or vision prerequisite, and accepts legitimate changes without direct fit.

Explain how the result meets the brief, what to inspect first and any directional change and reason, including consequential company evidence and unverified assumptions when applicable. Distinguish selected directions, provisional recommendations and deferred questions with their next tests. Any later authorized substantive revision needs accurate new revision/review coverage; preserve the bounded-repair stop. Start no subsequent work automatically.
